source_review.notes: Checked current Linux blk-mq, stable sysfs ABI, block statistics, I/O statistics, pressure, tracepoint, io_uring and io_uring setup documentation plus current fio and block-subsystem documentation. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; kernel interfaces, queueing identities, illustrative calculations, operational recommendations and assurance remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked arrival, completion, response, service, wait, throughput, occupancy, payload, bandwidth, utilization, demand, capacity, batch, deadline and miss notation.
Reviewed latency decomposition, Little's Law, useful bandwidth, resource-demand bound, deadline-miss ratio and count-or-time batch trigger.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates time, rate, bytes, occupancy, capacity and indicators and explicitly limits equations to compatible boundaries and stated assumptions.

evidence: Recomputed 100,000 operations per second times 200 microseconds as average occupancy 20.
Executed four operating points and confirmed occupancies 6.0, 20.0, 60.0 and 108.9 and selection of the highest rate meeting a 500-microsecond p99 target.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates unit conversion and selection from four observations only; it does not predict a device, arrival distribution, percentile or production operating point.

evidence: Re-derived response as waiting plus service and average occupancy as completion rate times mean residence time for one boundary.
Checked useful-byte rate, normalized resource-demand throughput bound and deadline indicator aggregation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are accounting and capacity models, not claims of exponential queueing, independent service, stationary percentiles or universal saturation behavior.

evidence: Reviewed zero and low arrival rates, saturation, unbounded admission, size-only batching, maximum depth, missing completions, late completions, cancellation races and retries.
Reviewed cache effects, long-run drift, remote NUMA, shared locks, mixed tenants, write interference, device reset, path loss, resource exhaustion, open-loop overload and generator backlog.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Semantic, time-boundary, queue, lifecycle, topology, workload, fairness, failure, measurement and assurance boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced arrival, admission, submission, publication, device work, completion, wakeup, timeout, cancellation, retry, reset and failover through twelve obligations.
Verified semantic equivalence, consistent measurement, bounded queues, safe publication, exactly-once termination, deadline boundaries, recovery reserve and topology alignment.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats throughput, latency, correctness, ownership, fairness, locality, backpressure and recovery as coupled but independently testable invariants.

evidence: Reviewed contracts, latency components, percentiles, Little's Law, bottlenecks, queues, admission, synchronous and asynchronous I/O, batching, copies, DMA, interrupts, polling, scheduling and experiments.

Constructed counterexamples for device-as-end-to-end latency, maximum-depth-as-optimum, more-queues-as-no-contention, timeout-as-stopped-I/O, utilization-as-throughput and closed-loop-as-overload evidence.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable design and validation obligations, not a formal proof of Linux, io_uring, blk-mq, a scheduler, device, workload, SLO or capacity plan.

evidence: Audited uses of admitted, submitted, issued, completed, durable, saturated, bounded, fair, optimal, cancelled, retried, reset and recovered.
Confirmed kernel contracts, queueing identities, measured examples, recommendations, experiments and assurance claims remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Device completion is not labeled application completion, average accounting is not labeled tail prediction, hardware capacity is not labeled optimal depth and process timeout is not labeled access containment.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-070/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the operating-point calculation.
Reviewed required workload, arrival, admission, queue, CPU, topology, trace, histogram, durability, error, retry, reset, environment and raw-evidence fields.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes arithmetic over four supplied points only; it provides no evidence for a Linux kernel, storage device, polling path, queue controller, SLO, failure response or production workload.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed semantics, latency budgets, useful throughput, queueing, admission, completion strategies, topology, scheduling, durability, recovery, workloads and evidence as one end-to-end path design.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current Linux and fio mechanisms as implementable concerns, including queue inventory, polling, stable tunables, pressure, trace correlation, resource reserves, open-loop overload and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from contracts and measurement through queue, data-path and completion design, then recovery and experiments, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-four misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux block, io_uring, storage-vendor, queueing-theory, performance, reliability, security, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
